translations.literal: Now you, sir, have had the fortune to roam in an age of emperors and kings, personally to wear the cap-strings and robes of office, to float amid brilliance and steep yourself in the Way and virtue, to gaze long on the patterns of dragon and tiger—this has gone on long.
translations.idiomatic: You live under an enlightened throne, wear court regalia, swim in culture and soak in the Way, and have long feasted your eyes on imperial portents.

sentences.zh: 卒不能攄首尾，奮翼鱗，振拔洿塗，跨騰風雲，使見之者景駭，聞之者嚮震。

translations.literal: Yet in the end you cannot spread head and tail, flap scales and fins, struggle free of the mire, leap through wind and cloud, so that those who see you stand awestruck and those who hear you turn in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you never spread wings from the mud or ride the tempest so that sight of you would stagger the world.

sentences.zh: 徒樂枕經籍書，紆體衡門，上無所蔕，下無所根。

translations.literal: You merely delight in pillowing your head on the classics and histories, folding your limbs within a plain gate, with nothing above to cling to and nothing below to root you.
translations.idiomatic: You hug your books beneath a humble gate, tethered neither to high office nor to solid ground.

sentences.zh: 獨攄意虖宇宙之外，銳思於豪芒之內，潛神默記，恆以年歲。

translations.literal: Alone you let your thoughts wander beyond the cosmos and hone them finer than a hair's tip; you sink your spirit in silent memorization year after year.
translations.idiomatic: You send the mind past the sky while polishing thoughts on a pinpoint, brooding in silence year on year.

sentences.zh: 然而器不賈於當己，用不效於一世， 雖馳辯如濤波，摛藻如春華，猶無益於殿最。

translations.literal: Yet your vessel is not priced in the market of the moment, your use is not tested in a single generation; though your disputation surges like breakers and your phrases unfold like spring blossoms, it still does no good in the ranking of first and last."
translations.idiomatic: Still your talent finds no buyer today, your use no proof in this life; torrents of eloquence and springtime rhetoric win you no place in the merit roll."

sentences.zh: 意者，且運朝夕之策，定合會之計，使存有顯號，亡有美諡，不亦優虖？」

translations.literal: Perhaps you should instead ply morning-and-evening stratagems, fix plans for alliance and conference, so that the living win glorious titles and the dead fair posthumous names—would that not be better?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not scheme for office and alliance so the living gain rank and the dead fine posthumous names—would that not be wiser?"

sentences.zh: 主人逌爾而咲曰：「若賓之言，斯所謂見勢利之華，闇道德之實，守穾奧之熒燭，未卬天庭而睹白日也。

translations.literal: The host smiled faintly and said, "If that is your doctrine, it is what people call seeing the flowers of power and profit while blind to the fruit of the Way, guarding a guttering candle in a corner and never lifting your eyes to the celestial court to behold the bright sun.
translations.idiomatic: The host smiled and said such talk mistakes glitter for the Way, like nursing a candle in a cellar while the sun blazes overhead.

sentences.zh: 曩者王塗蕪穢，周失其御，侯伯方軌，戰國橫騖，於是七雄虓闞，分裂諸夏，龍戰而虎爭。

translations.literal: Formerly the royal highways were choked with weeds, Zhou lost the reins, marquises ran on parallel tracks, the Warring States raced crosswise; then the seven champions roared and wrestled, split the central states, and dragon fought with tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Once royal roads rotted, Zhou lost control, barons raced abreast, and the seven powers tore China in a war of dragon and tiger.

sentences.zh: 游說之徒，風颺電激，並起而救之，其餘猋飛景附，煜霅其間者，蓋不可勝載。

translations.literal: Wandering persuaders, swift as wind and lightning, rose together to rescue the age; the rest, like gales and flying shadows attaching themselves, flashed among them in numbers no carriage could carry.
translations.idiomatic: Rhetoricians stormed in like wind and lightning, and hangers-on swarmed beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，搦朽摩鈍，鈆刀皆能壹斷，是故魯連飛一矢而蹶千金，虞卿以顧眄而捐相印也。

translations.literal: In such a time, even a rotten twig or a dull blade could cut clean at one stroke; therefore Lu Zhonglian loosed a single arrow and toppled a thousand pounds of gold, and Yu Qing, with a glance, cast away the minister's seal."
translations.idiomatic: In that chaos a blunt knife could decide a fate, so Lu Zhonglian felled a fortune with one shaft and Yu Qing dropped a premier's seal at a glance."

sentences.zh: 夫啾發投曲，感耳之聲，合之律度，淫䵷而不可聽者，非韶、夏之樂也；

translations.literal: For twittering runs and tossed-off tunes that please the ear yet, set beside pitch and measure, prove lewd and unfit to hear—that is not the music of Shao and Xia;
translations.idiomatic: Shrill novelty may please the ear yet fail the scale—that is not the music of Shao and Xia;

sentences.zh: 因勢合變，偶時之會，風移俗易，乖忤而不可通者，非君子之法也。

translations.literal: for opportunism that rides the moment, suits passing fashion, shifts custom, and ends in perverse blockage—that is not the gentleman's law."
translations.idiomatic: and tactics that chase fashion until custom warps are not the gentleman's law."

sentences.zh: 及至從人合之，衡人散之，亡命漂說，羇旅騁辭，商鞅挾三術以鑽孝公，李斯奮時務而要始皇，彼皆躡風雲之會，履顛沛之勢，據徼乘邪以求一日之富貴，朝為榮華，夕而焦瘁，福不盈眥，禍益於世，凶人且以自悔，況吉士而是賴虖！

translations.literal: Down to the verticalists who united others and the horizontalists who split them, men who risked life on drifting persuasion or peddled rhetoric as exiles—Shang Yang brought three arts to bore into Duke Xiao, Li Si seized the pressing task to corner the First Emperor—they all trod the meeting of wind and cloud, walked the verge of overturn, clung to narrow chances and rode crooked ways to snatch a day's wealth and honor: morning brought glory, evening brought charred ruin; blessing did not fill an eyeblink, disaster overflowed the age; evil men repented even themselves—how much less should the good rely on that path!"
translations.idiomatic: Think of vertical and horizontal schemers, exiled tongues, Shang Yang's triple trick on Duke Xiao, Li Si's grab at Qin's moment—they rode storm and crisis, gambled on crooked odds, blazed one dawn and burned by dusk; rogues rued it—should an honest man copy them?"

sentences.zh: 且功不可以虛成，名不可以偽立，韓設辯以徼君，呂行詐以賈國。

translations.literal: Moreover merit cannot be hollowly achieved, nor name falsely erected: Han Fei set sophistry to hook his ruler, Lü Buwei practiced fraud to traffic in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Merit cannot be faked nor name bought: Han Fei angled his prince with rhetoric, Lü Buwei sold the realm by deceit.

sentences.zh: 說難既酋，其身乃囚；

translations.literal: When the "Difficulty of Persuasion" was finished, his person was imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: Han Fei finished his essay on persuasion and landed in prison;

sentences.zh: 秦貨既貴，厥宗亦隧。

translations.literal: when Qin's bribe had grown costly, his clan too went down the tunnel.
translations.idiomatic: when Lü's price for Qin rose, his house followed him into the grave.

sentences.zh: 是故仲尼抗浮雲之志，孟軻養浩然之氣，彼豈樂為迂闊哉？

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongni set his will above drifting clouds, and Meng Ke nurtured the flood-like qi—did they delight in being impractical?
translations.idiomatic: So Confucius fixed his mind above the clouds and Mencius fed the flood-like breath—were they merely eccentric?

sentences.zh: 道不可以貳也。

translations.literal: The Way does not admit doubleness."
translations.idiomatic: The Way allows no divided loyalty."

sentences.zh: 方今大漢洒埽群穢，夷險芟荒，廓帝紘，恢皇綱，基隆於羲、農，規廣於黃、唐；

translations.literal: Now the great Han has swept away every stain, leveled peril, mowed the wilds, spread the imperial cord, widened the royal net; its foundation rises higher than Xi and Nong, its compass vaster than Huang and Tang;
translations.idiomatic: Great Han has cleansed the mire, cut the brambles, stretched the emperor's net wider than Fu Xi or Shen Nong, vaster than Huangdi or Yao;

sentences.zh: 其君天下也，炎之如日，威之如神，函之如海，養之如春。

translations.literal: in ruling all under Heaven it blazes like the sun, awes like a spirit, embraces like the sea, nurtures like spring.
translations.idiomatic: its rule warms like the sun, awes like a god, holds all like the sea, and quickens like spring.

sentences.zh: 是以六合之內，莫不同原共流，沐浴玄德，稟卬太和，枝附葉著，譬猶屮木之殖山林，鳥魚之毓川澤，得氣者蕃滋，失時者苓落，參天墬而施化，豈云人事之厚薄哉？

translations.literal: Therefore within the six coordinates none fail to share one source and one current, bathe in dark virtue, drink deep of supreme harmony, cling like branches and leaves; they are like plants growing in mountain forests, birds and fish breeding in rivers and marshes—those who catch the vapor flourish and multiply, those who miss the season wither and fall; Heaven and earth join to spread transformation—how can one speak of human affairs being thick or thin?"
translations.idiomatic: Within the six directions all drink one stream, bathe in hidden virtue, and cling like leaves to a tree; timing makes the growth, heaven and earth do the shaping—human whim weighs little."

sentences.zh: 今子處皇世而論戰國，耀所聞而疑所覿，欲從旄敦而度高虖泰山，懷氿濫而測深虖重淵，亦未至也。」

translations.literal: Now you, sir, stand in a brilliant age yet discourse on the Warring States, dazzle yourself with hearsay and doubt what your eyes see; you would measure Mount Tai with a yardstick from Dunhuang or fathom the abyss with a puddle from a marsh—you have not reached the mark."
translations.idiomatic: You judge a golden age by Warring States gossip, like gauging Tai Shan with a desert foot-rule or sounding the deep with ditch water."

sentences.zh: 賓曰：「若夫鞅、斯之倫，衰周之凶人，既聞命矣。

translations.literal: The guest said, "As for men like Shang Yang and Li Si, villains of failing Zhou—I have heard your command.
translations.idiomatic: The guest bowed to his lecture on Shang Yang and Li Si, villains of a dying age.

sentences.zh: 敢問上古之士，處身行道，輔世成名，可述於後者，默而已虖？」

translations.literal: May I ask: among men of high antiquity who kept their persons, practiced the Way, aided the age, and won names handed down—did they stay silent?"
translations.idiomatic: But did the ancients who kept the Way, aided their times, and left great names do it in silence?"

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「何為其然也！

translations.literal: The host said, "Why should it be so?
translations.idiomatic: The host answered, "Why imagine such a thing?

sentences.zh: 昔咎繇謨虞，箕子訪周，言通帝王，謀合聖神；

translations.literal: Formerly Gao Yao counseled Yu, Jizi was questioned in Zhou—their words penetrated emperors and kings, their plans matched sages and spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao advised Yu, Jizi counseled Zhou—their speech reached kings, their plans matched the spirits;

sentences.zh: 殷說夢發於傅巖，周望兆動於渭濱，齊甯激聲於康衢，漢良受書於邳沂，皆俟命而神交，匪詞言之所信，故能建必然之策，展無窮之勳也。

translations.literal: Yin's dream revelation came from Fu Yue's cliff, Zhou's hopeful omen stirred by the Wei bank, Ning Qi's song rang from the broad crossroads, Zhang Liang received his book beside the Yi of Pei—all awaited fate and communed with spirits, not mere words to be trusted; therefore they could lay inevitable strategies and unfold endless merit."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yue rose from a cliff dream, Lü Wang from the Wei shallows, Ning Qi from a roadside song, Zhang Liang from a book at dawn—they waited Heaven's nod, not rhetoric, and so built lasting deeds."

sentences.zh: 近者陸子優繇，新語以興；

translations.literal: In recent times Master Lu, leisurely and easy, raised the New Discourses to prominence;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia, calm and unhurried, raised the New Discourses;

sentences.zh: 董生下帷，發藻儒林；

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu let down his curtain and sent brilliance through the Confucian grove;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu drew his curtain and lit the grove of scholars;

sentences.zh: 劉向司籍，辯章舊聞；

translations.literal: Liu Xiang superintended the registers and sorted the old hearsay;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang ordered the archives and clarified antiquity;

sentences.zh: 揚雄覃思，法言、大玄：皆及時君之門闈，究先聖之壼奧，婆娑虖術藝之場，休息虖篇籍之囿，以全其質而發其文，用納虖聖聽，列炳於後人，斯非其亞與！

translations.literal: Yang Xiong pondered deeply and produced the Model Sayings and the Great Mystery: all reached the inner gates of the timely ruler, fathomed the inner rooms of former sages, wandered in the arena of arts, rested in the park of writings, thereby preserving their substance and releasing their pattern, were taken into the sage's hearing, and blaze in rows for later men—are these not next after the highest?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong brooded out the Model Sayings and Great Arcana; each entered the ruler's gate, sounded the sages' chambers, ranged the field of learning, and left texts that shine for posterity—second only to the greatest."

sentences.zh: 若乃夷抗行於首陽，惠降志於辱仕，顏耽樂於簞瓢，孔終篇於西狩，聲盈塞於天淵，真吾徒之師表也。

translations.literal: Or again there were those who set pure conduct on Shouyang, Hui who lowered his will to a humbling office, Yan who took joy in a single basket and gourd, Confucius who finished his classic at the western hunt—their fame filled the gulf between Heaven and abyss; they are true models for our kind."
translations.idiomatic: Think of Yi and Shu on Shouyang, Hui in a low post, Yan with his single meal, Confucius closing the Spring and Autumn at the western hunt—their names shook heaven and earth; they are our true exemplars."

sentences.zh: 且吾聞之：壹陰壹陽，天墬之方；

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard: one yin, one yang—this is Heaven and earth's square;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that yin and yang are the square of heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 乃文乃質，王道之綱；

translations.literal: both pattern and substance—this is the kingly Way's cord;
translations.idiomatic: culture and substance are the twin cords of the kingly Way;

sentences.zh: 有同有異，聖喆之常。

translations.literal: having sameness and having difference—this is the constant of the wise and good."
translations.idiomatic: sameness and difference are the sage's constant scales."

sentences.zh: 故曰：慎修所志，守爾天符，委命共己，味道之腴，神之聽之，名其舍諸！

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: carefully cultivate what you aim at, guard your Heaven-given tally, entrust life to what is already in yourself, taste the richness of the Way; when the spirits listen, will fame leave you?"
translations.idiomatic: The ode says: polish your purpose, keep Heaven's tally, yield life to what is already yours, taste the Way's fat—when spirits listen, can fame stay away?"

sentences.zh: 賓又不聞龢氏之璧韞於荊石，隨侯之珠藏於蜯蛤虖？

translations.literal: Again, have you not heard that the He clan jade was wrapped in a Jing stone, or that the Marquis of Sui's pearl lay hidden in a mussel?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you never heard how the He-bi jade slept inside a dull rock or Sui's pearl hid in a shell?"

sentences.zh: 歷世莫眡，不知其將含景耀，吐英精，曠千載而流夜光也。

translations.literal: Age after age none saw them, not knowing they would hold radiant light and spit essence, idle a thousand years yet shed light by night.
translations.idiomatic: Ages passed before anyone knew they would blaze with inner fire and gleam in the dark after a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 應龍潛於潢汙，魚黿媟之，不睹其能奮靈德，合風雲，超忽荒，而躆顥蒼也。

translations.literal: The responding dragon lurked in a muddy pool; fish and turtles despised him, not seeing how he could rouse numinous virtue, join wind and cloud, leap beyond the vast waste, and stand in the azure sky.
translations.idiomatic: The winged dragon wallowed in a puddle while minnows mocked him, blind to the day he would ride the storm into the blue.

sentences.zh: 故夫泥蟠而天飛者，應龍之神也；

translations.literal: Therefore one who coils in the mud yet flies to Heaven is the spirit of the responding dragon;
translations.idiomatic: Mud-bound yet sky-soaring—that is the responding dragon;

sentences.zh: 先賤而後貴者，龢、隨之珍也；

translations.literal: one who is base first and honored later is the treasure of He and Sui;
translations.idiomatic: cheap at first, costly later—that is the He jade and Sui pearl;

sentences.zh: 時闇而久章者，君子之真也。

translations.literal: one who is dim for a time yet shines long is the truth of the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: long hidden, long bright—that is the gentleman's truth."

sentences.zh: 若乃牙、曠清耳於管絃，離婁眇目於豪分；

translations.literal: If then Ya and Kuang clear their ears to strings and pipes, and Li Lou strains his eyes to a hair's fraction;
translations.idiomatic: When Ya and Kuang tune their ears to music, or Li Lou splits a hair's breadth;

sentences.zh: 逢蒙絕技於弧矢，班輸榷巧於斧斤；

translations.literal: Peng Meng exhausts his skill on bow and arrow, Lu Ban measures his craft on axe and adze;
translations.idiomatic: when Peng Meng masters the bow or Lu Ban the adze;

sentences.zh: 良樂軼能於相馭，烏獲抗力於千鈞；

translations.literal: Wang Liang and Bo Le surpass others in judging and driving, Wu Huo matches strength against a thousand jun;
translations.idiomatic: when Wang Liang and Bo Le judge horses or Wu Huo hefts a thousand jun;

sentences.zh: 龢、鵲發精於鍼石，研、桑心計於無垠。

translations.literal: Bian Que and Hua Tuo bring essence to needle and stone, Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang reckon profit in the boundless.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que and Hua Tuo wield the needle with spirit, while Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang calculate gain across the boundless market.

sentences.zh: 僕亦不任廁技於彼列，故密爾自娛於斯文。」

translations.literal: I, your servant, am not fit to crowd my petty skill among them; therefore I quietly take my pleasure in this writing.
translations.idiomatic: I am not fit to stack my small talent beside theirs, so I take quiet joy in these words alone.
